streaming.simple: Processing data one value at a time, with fixed memory, without storing the whole history.
streaming.example: A running average of sensor readings.

online algorithm.simple: An algorithm that updates its answer for each new value instead of recomputing from scratch.

catastrophic cancellation.simple: A big loss of precision when you subtract two large, almost equal floating-point numbers.

Welford's algorithm.simple: A stable one-pass method to compute the mean and variance of a stream.

deque.simple: A double-ended queue: you can add and remove at both ends in constant time.

monotonic deque.simple: A deque whose values are always sorted (for example decreasing). Used to track a window maximum.

window.simple: A fixed number of the most recent points of a series.

heap.simple: A tree-like structure that gives the smallest (min-heap) or largest (max-heap) item fast.

lazy deletion.simple: Do not remove an item at once. Mark it, and remove it later when it reaches the top.
lazy deletion.example: A dictionary of values to delete.

median filter.simple: Smoothing where each point becomes the median of a window around it. It removes spikes.
median filter.example: Window of 5 to remove single-point glitches.

EWMA.simple: Exponentially weighted moving average: a smooth value where new data get weight alpha and the old estimate gets 1 - alpha.

rate limiting.simple: Allowing only a fixed number of requests in a period of time.

token bucket.simple: A rate limiter with tokens that refill at a steady rate up to a capacity. A request spends tokens.

bucket.simple: A fixed time interval used to group events, such as one minute.
bucket.example: Timestamps 120 to 179 s are in the bucket that starts at 120.

session.simple: A group of events by one user with no long pause between neighbouring events.
session.example: Clicks of one visit to a website.

sessionization.simple: Splitting an event log into sessions.
sessionization.example: A gap over 30 minutes starts a new session.

island.simple: A block of consecutive items, for example days in a row with a login.
island.example: Logins on 1, 2, 3 May form an island.

gap.simple: A break between islands: a missing step.

streak.simple: The length of a run of consecutive days (or steps) with an event.

downsampling.simple: Reducing the number of points of a series, for example to draw a chart.

LTTB.simple: Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets: a downsampling method that keeps the visual shape of a series.
LTTB.example: Used by chart libraries for big time series.

window function.simple: A SQL function that computes a value for each row from a set of related rows, without collapsing the rows.

frame.simple: The set of rows around the current row that a window function uses.
frame.example: ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.

running total.simple: A cumulative sum: for each row, the sum from the first row to this row.

CTE.simple: Common table expression: a named temporary result at the top of a query, written with WITH.

recursive CTE.simple: A CTE that refers to itself to produce rows step by step, for example one row per day.

COALESCE.simple: A SQL function that returns the first value that is not NULL.

rolling window.simple: The last k points of a series. It moves forward one step at a time.

variance.simple: The average squared distance of the values from their mean. The square root is the standard deviation.

timestamp.simple: A number or text that says when an event happened.

NULL.example: LAG on the first row gives NULL.

tie-breaker.simple: An extra sort key that picks one row when two rows are equal on the main key.

cumulative sum.simple: A running total: each value is the sum of all values so far.

O(n).simple: Linear time: the work grows in proportion to the input size n.
